methods.label: Fix the hundreds digit
methods.sourceMethod: The references reduce the reversal condition to a hundreds digit of 5 and count bounded multiples of 7. The AoPS note also informs the explicit treatment of a leading zero after reversal.

annotationRationale: The decisive ideas are the last-digit test for divisibility by 5 and counting integer multipliers in a bounded interval. The supplied digit-by-digit congruence route adds unnecessary casework to this short problem.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The answer is 14, choice B, when a reversed digit string denotes its integer value. Thus 560 reverses to 65 and qualifies. AoPS records a leading-zero concern, but the question requires only N to have three digits. No explicit disputed or voided grading status, figure, or other contradiction is supplied.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The supplied congruence casework offers no useful additional insight for this short interval count. One method is sufficient.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed last-digit test and bounded integer count match the solution. Empty support and contextual roles are reasonable.
review.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The reversal condition forces the hundreds digit to be 5. The neighboring excluded multiples are 497 and 602, so the eligible multipliers are exactly 72 through 85, giving 85-72+1=14. Including 560 is consistent with the stated integer interpretation; excluding it would give 13.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Both cited third-party references support this reduction and count, and the AoPS note supports discussing 560. The source-informed-original designation is honest; the standard mathematical statements and independently expanded explanation do not show copied prose.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first move, interval endpoints, inclusive count, and leading-zero convention are explained clearly enough to reconstruct without a figure.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_p154 supplies precisely the divisibility-by-5 test used. cnm_h020 fits counting the bounded integer multipliers. Neither ID is unsupported.
